claim: Active inference treats reward as one more observation with a prior preference; flattening the preference removes any pull toward reward (null agent scores 50.03 deterministic and 50.22 stochastic in FrozenLake, chance).
agent_test: Background only; not a scaffold part.

claim: In tiny discrete FrozenLake, active inference (99.88 deterministic, 98.90 stochastic) equals or beats Bayesian model-based RL (99.76, 64.39) and Q-learning (eps 0.1: 97.79 and 66.08; decaying eps: 80.44 and 65.13). The stochastic gap is large but rests on one paper with naive RL baselines.
agent_test: Hidden-switch text world: agent with an explicit context belief vs plain memory agent, equal tokens.

claim: After a hidden goal swap, active inference recovered in one episode while Q-learning and Bayesian RL needed about 40. The gain comes from a model with an explicit 'context switched' hypothesis; the authors say a richer RL agent could match it.
agent_test: Change the task rule mid-session; count steps to recover with vs without a written 'rule may have changed' hypothesis.

claim: With no reward at all, Q-learning learns nothing (score 0, 15 moves, circular policy) while belief-based agents keep exploring (Bayesian RL 39.94, active inference 44.00). Exploring without reward needs an uncertainty term.
agent_test: In open mode, isolated attempts with a code-kept coverage tracker vs without, equal tokens, score distinct valid outputs.

claim: Reward shaping barely moves Bayesian RL and active inference (99.5 to 99.9, about 3.0 moves) but moves Q-learning (95.3 to 96.5, 3.4 to 3.6 moves). With only a negative preference all three agents avoid the hole and never reach the goal (score 0, 15 moves).
agent_test: Check that an avoid-errors-only objective stalls the agent; keep a positive goal check at S8.

claim: Learned preferences can lock in bad goals: an agent that hits the hole first comes to prefer holes (about 5 trials). Preference learning without an anchor is unsafe.
agent_test: Let the agent revise its own success criterion from early outputs and measure drift in accuracy.

claim: Active inference with epistemic value handles sparse reward: FEEF reached optimal Mountain Car in one trial while reward-only baselines mostly failed, and covered reward-free Ant Maze more than random (35 episodes, 4 seeds).
agent_test: A sparse-success task where random attempts rarely succeed: coverage tracker vs none, equal tokens.

claim: Boundary: directed exploration adds nothing when random actions already reach the goal (Cup Catch: all agents converge in about 20 episodes).
agent_test: Skip diversity machinery on easy items; compare accuracy and tokens.

claim: On shaped-reward continuous control, model-based active inference is about 10x more sample efficient than model-free DDPG (under 100 epochs vs 1500). This is a model-based gain using only the extrinsic term, not evidence for the epistemic term.
agent_test: Different axis (model-based vs model-free); not testable on a scaffold.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Deep active inference gains often come from entropy or the model, not the epistemic term: on CartPole most of the gain came from the entropy term (reward 500), and epistemic value had no measurable effect on CartPole, Acrobot or Lunar Lander.
agent_test: Ablate an information-gain prompt against a plain 'try something different' prompt at equal tokens.

claim: Deep active inference on dSprites does not reproduce as an EFE minimiser (Champion 2024): only reward-maximising variants solve it, EFE agents pick nearly one action, and 1% information gain added after 200K steps drastically cuts reward. This contradicts the original positive reports.
agent_test: Mix an information-gain objective into a reward-driven loop at several weights; watch accuracy.

claim: Fountas 2020 reports an MCTS deep active inference agent matched reward-only agents on reward while exploring more, and beat DQN and A2C and matched PPO2 on Animal-AI at 2M iterations (authors call these illustrations); Champion 2024 disputes the mechanism.
agent_test: None direct.

claim: Theory: standard discrete active inference is Bellman-optimal only at horizon 1; sophisticated inference (recursive) recovers backward induction at any finite horizon, for known finite-horizon models.
agent_test: One-shot whole-plan choice vs recursive step-by-step planning on multi-step items, equal tokens.

claim: Theory: the expected free energy is not just the free energy of the future (the natural version discourages information seeking), and active inference and control-as-inference differ in where value enters (prior vs likelihood) and in which information terms they keep.
agent_test: Theory only.
audit_note: Both statements verified (EFE 'not simply free energy in the future' and natural version discourages exploration; AIF vs CAI value in prior vs likelihood, AIF keeps epistemic info gain CAI lacks), but all sources are one lab (Millidge, Tschantz, Buckley, Seth), so it is a single-group theoretical position.

claim: A bound ties EFE policies to Bayes-optimal RL: regret gap linear in horizon and quadratic in information gain, with reward and information gain balanced by a temperature.
agent_test: Sweep exploration weight by difficulty.

claim: Reward-free preference learning shows an inverted U with environment volatility: exploration peaks at 50% volatility and collapses to bimodal preferences (noisy-TV-like) at 100%.
agent_test: Vary how much the task keeps changing; check diversity does not chase noise.

claim: Contrastive active inference (no pixel likelihood) matches reward-based RL on image tasks; likelihood-based active inference failed to converge on Reacher.
agent_test: None direct.

claim: Language models do not explore well by default: GPT-4 bandit exploration worked in only one scaffolded configuration (suggestive framing, summarised history, reinforced chain of thought, temperature 0); the basic prompt had suffix failures in over 60% of 20 replicates at T=500. Gap search: code-computed summary and exploration statistics lift Gemini Pro bandit win-rate from 45.5 (raw history) to 59.6-60.0 and contextual-bandit from 7.1 to 64.3 (EVOLvE); small Gemma models gain nothing.
agent_test: Code-kept history of tried directions vs raw-context history, equal tokens.
audit_note: Krishnamurthy et al. (one configuration works; >60% suffix failures with basic prompt, T=500, N=20) and EVOLvE Table 1 (MAB 45.5->60.0/59.6, CB 7.1->64.3) match; 'small Gemma models gain nothing' is slightly loose (Gemma-2B got a small gain from summarized history, none from algorithm-guided support).

claim: GPT-3 shows random but no directed exploration (horizon effect beta=-0.15+-0.27, p=.58) yet beats humans on regret (2.72 vs 3.24), so good reward can hide missing information seeking.
agent_test: Measure distinctness separately from accuracy; do not infer exploration from score.

claim: An LLM agent with a reward-free exploration curriculum (Voyager) beat ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT on Minecraft tech-tree speed (wooden tool 6+-2 vs 92+-72 iterations; diamond 1/3), while ReAct and Reflexion unlocked no tech level (0/3). Only 3 runs per method. Voyager ablations: random curriculum cuts items by 93%, no self-verification by 73%, no skill library plateaus late; not matched for tokens.
agent_test: Code-driven curriculum assigning untried directions vs free self-prompting, equal tokens.

claim: Exploration bonuses help even when reward exists in LLM training: a perplexity bonus raised Qwen3-4B GRPO AIME24 20.8 to 23.3, AIME25 21.0 to 23.5, average 48.2 to 50.6; an information-gain reward helped multi-turn personalisation.
agent_test: Training evidence; no direct scaffold test.
audit_note: CDE Table 1 (Qwen3-4B-Base GRPO vs PPL bonus: 20.8->23.3, 21.0->23.5, avg 48.2->50.6) matches; the curiosity-reward dialogue paper rewards user-model accuracy (never says 'information gain' explicitly) and reports no numbers checked here.

claim: LLM-agent uses of active inference are weakly validated: Prakki 2025 reports no baseline comparison, Wen 2025 papers report no experiments; only PUMA (2026) reports measured gains in a simulator (Stage Lift 1.62 vs 1.07, Prep 75.9% vs 52.0%, Qwen3-8B vs DIIR). Dutta 2026 (2608.19202) is a framework paper with a dynamic-programming oracle comparison and a no-question baseline in its clarification experiment, but no direct with/without active-inference prompt comparison on the main question-asking task. (BED-LLM update not verified here.)
agent_test: EFE-style choice of next question vs plain clarifying question, equal tokens.
audit_note: PUMA numbers (Qwen3-8B 1.62 vs 1.07, 75.9% vs 52.0%, DynPatient simulator), Prakki (no baseline) and Wen (conceptual) verified; but Dutta et al. Section 7 does include a no-question 'baseline' policy, so 'no plain-prompt baseline' is too strong; BED-LLM/K24 update not checked against any listed source.
claim_before_audit: LLM-agent uses of active inference are weakly validated: Prakki 2025 reports no baseline, Wen 2025 papers report no experiments; only PUMA (2026) reports measured gains in a simulator (Stage Lift 1.62 vs 1.07, Prep 75.9% vs 52.0%, 8B models). Update: BED-LLM (ICLR 2026) now gives a measured gain for information-gain question choice in LLMs (see K24), and Dutta 2026 (2608.19202) is an opened framework paper with an oracle comparison but no plain-prompt baseline.

claim: Choosing actions by expected information gain improved user-state tracking for small models: CAMI next-state accuracy 0.717 vs 0.231 for a long-prompt baseline; Qwen3-8B PUMA beat long-prompt Qwen3-32B on AnnoMI (0.639 and 0.532 vs 0.602 and 0.430).
agent_test: On underspecified items pick the clarifying question by expected information gain, equal tokens.

claim: Choosing the next question by estimated expected information gain over a code-kept hypothesis list beats a plain 'ask an informative question' prompt in LLM 20 Questions: final success is typically more than double (Animals: Mistral-Large 33 to 95, Llama-3.1-8B 8 to 63, GPT-4o 45 to 93; 100 targets per set). Most of the gain needs filtering of inconsistent hypotheses; even-split alone gets 85-87 on Qwen Animals vs 95; chain-of-thought alone 51.
agent_test: Hidden-target text game: EIG-over-hypothesis-list probe vs 'try something different' prompt, equal tokens (BED-LLM did not match tokens).

claim: Boundary: the information-gain benefit shrinks when the target is vague. In film-preference elicitation Prompt-Only is a strong baseline and BED-LLM's boost is smaller; updating the likelihood with full history did not help (Animals GPT-4o 93 vs 86).
agent_test: Apply the probe operator only where the hypothesis space is crisp; otherwise plain prompting is competitive.

claim: Noisy-TV defence: reward learning progress (change in model error), not prediction error. In stochastic MountainCar coverage drops 12.4% for learning-progress monitoring against 33-86% for ensemble, RND, IDF and others. No LLM test of a code-side version exists.
agent_test: Stop or switch a probe direction when the last K answers did not change the hypothesis set; compare with surprise-seeking probes on a task with a random-answer source.

claim: Token-aware stop rule for asking: ask the attribute with the largest entropy per token and stop under a threshold. In a 48-task simulation the tuned rule (threshold 0.01, max 2 questions) reached 0.375 verifier compliance at about 219 tokens vs 0.0417 at about 112 tokens for no questions. Small, templated, simulated answers.
agent_test: Cap probes per item and stop when expected information per token falls under a tuned threshold.

claim: Without an explicit change hypothesis, frontier LLMs adapt slowly after a hidden reversal: post-reversal perseveration 7.2-10.9 trials (Gemini-3, GPT-5.2) and 19.6-27.4 (DeepSeek-V3.2) against 2.9 for humans (N=200 runs per cell). Whether a written 'context switched' hypothesis fixes this is untested.
agent_test: Mid-task rule change: scaffold with an explicit 'did the rule change' test vs plain memory, count trials to recover.

claim: Self-written or same-model-judged objectives drift: in iterative self-refinement judge scores rise while human ratings stall (shared context drives it, larger models more), and better prompt specification does not remove in-context reward hacking. Only indirect support for a fixed-criterion guardrail, no controlled fixed-vs-self-written comparison.
agent_test: Fixed written success criterion plus a judge with separate context vs agent-edited criterion, count criterion drift over 10 rounds.

claim: Open gaps with no measured answer after this search: (a) FrozenLake result against a stronger RL baseline with explicit context belief, (b) usable rule linking Wei's regret bound to problem difficulty, (c) 2608.19202 compared against a plain-prompt baseline. Surprise-gated deliberation (d12) is self-reported on one scenario.
agent_test: Research backlog, not a scaffold part.
